message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the development of a mane in adult male individuals. The presence of a mane is governed by a dominant allele (often denoted as **M**), while its absence (no mane) is recessive (**m**). Thus, a male lion inherits at least one dominant allele from either parent and will develop a mane, whereas a female lion typically does not carry the dominant allele in a way that would produce a mane.
